facts.text: MoveJ creates the ROS 2 action server /MoveJ on the MoveJ_ActionServer node.
MoveJ.action declares a JointPose goal, a float64 speed, a string result and a string feedback.
JointPose.msg declares joint1 through joint6 as float64.
MoveJ multiplies each of the six goal joint values by k before assigning the MoveIt joint targets.
MoveJ defines the degree-to-radian constant k = pi/180.
MoveJ applies the goal speed with setMaxVelocityScalingFactor and 1.0 with setMaxAccelerationScalingFactor.
MoveJ checks each goal joint against per-robot degree limits selected by the ROB_PARAM string before planning; the irb120, irb1200, irb6640, cr35ia, ur3, ur5 and ur10 branches are present.
MoveJ plans with MoveIt, calls move(), then reports MoveJ:SUCCESS, MoveJ:FAILED or MoveJ:CANCELED; a planning failure still calls goal_handle->succeed with MoveJ:FAILED.
MoveJ's cancel handler calls move_group_interface.stop() and accepts the cancellation.
The MoveJ execute path checks is_canceling only after move() returns.
MoveJs creates the ROS 2 action server /MoveJs with a JointPoseS goal and a float64 speed.
MoveJs.action declares a JointPoseS goal, a float64 speed, a string result and a string feedback.
JointPoseS.msg declares joint1 through joint7 as float64.
MoveXYZ creates the ROS 2 action server /MoveXYZ and includes the generated MoveXYZ action header.
MoveXYZ sets an absolute target pose from positionx, positiony and positionz and keeps the current end-effector orientation.
MoveXYZ reports MoveXYZ:SUCCESS, MoveXYZ:FAILED or MoveXYZ:CANCELED, and a planning failure still succeeds the goal with MoveXYZ:FAILED.
MoveG creates the ROS 2 action server /MoveG and includes the generated MoveG action header.
MoveG checks the gripper goal against panda_gripper upper 0.04 and egp64 upper 0.025, both with lower 0.0, then assigns the goal to both gripper joints.
MoveG reports MoveG:SUCCESS, MoveG:FAILED or MoveG:CANCELED, and a planning failure still succeeds the goal with MoveG:FAILED.
The README states the speed value must be in (0, 1], with 1 the maximum velocity and 0 the invalid null velocity.
The README describes /MoveJ as the 6-DOF joint-waypoint action and /MoveJs as its 7-DOF variant.
The README describes the ROS 2 actions as executing robot and end-effector motions in Gazebo simulation.
The Attacher action loops until a cancel request or a String True on /ros2_Detach, and returns an empty result; it exposes no stop service or stop action.
The MoveJ server registration and cancel callback are its only stop-shaped control path: the callback calls move_group_interface.stop() and accepts cancellation.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned action terminals; no physics step, planning, trajectory execution, pacing or state hash is modelled

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS recording fake (no Gazebo or MoveIt physics)
gaps: the fake is a ROS-free recording transport: it answers the four declared ROS 2 action goals with canned terminals and runs no Gazebo world, MoveIt planner, controller or sensor
joint, Cartesian and gripper goals are not applied to any simulated robot state; the fake reports the upstream's success/failure result strings only
the upstream README's speed range and the server's per-robot joint and gripper limits are recorded as source facts, not as a fake motion envelope
the action servers' cancel callbacks are not modelled as an acknowledged stop; the fake has no hold/queue and completes a default goal immediately
no live ROS graph or rosbridge deployment was contacted; the package remains contract_checked and model-authored

safe_state.description: No acknowledged safe state is declared: the pinned action servers expose only a cancel callback that calls move_group_interface.stop(); action cancellation is not an acknowledged stop binding.
